 Sun 15 Nov 2026 , Men's One Day International Series - 2nd ODI Australia vs England (batting), in play Australia Australia In Play England England Yet to bat 255 -4 ( 40.4 ) England are 255 for 4 with 9.2 overs remaining Australia: yet to bat England innings: 255 for 4 from 40.4 overs, in play
 Live Reporting (active) 
 Scorecard 
 Summary
 Opener Banton hits 121 off 99 balls for England 
 Brook bowled cheaply trying to ramp pacey Meredith 
 Root (62) puts on 137 for second wicket with Banton 
 Ex-Australia bowler Sayers backs Khawaja & Warner on sandpapergate 
 Baker in for Overton; Australia rest Beardman
 Australia win toss in second of three ODIs, Adelaide

 by Sam Drury
 Post published at 06:38 GMT 06:38 GMT 
 Michael Vaughan 
Former England captain on Test Match Special 
 England have a habit of not quite getting the total they want by being a bit too expansive.
 They do have the ability to get big scores, but I guess sometimes when you have done it once you can do it again. But we have all seen enough international cricket to know that's not possible.
 0 0 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Eng 245-4 published at 40 overs 40 overs 
 Six from Cooper Connolly's over and with 10 overs of the innings remaining, England have the platform to go big.
 They should get to 300 without too much trouble from here, can they get up to 330 or even 350? It's a big ask but not completely out of reach if these two stick around.
 0 0 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 06:34 GMT 06:34 GMT 
 Image source, Sir William Hoste CC My colleague, Timothy Abraham, disputes that the Adelaide Oval (see 06:20) has the greatest scoreboard in world cricket. 
 He insists it's on the Croatian island of Vis, where Sir William Hoste CC use converted wine barrels in a ground located in a vineyard.

 Eng 239-4 published at 39 overs 39 overs 
 Top shot!
 Will Jacks moves to leg to give himself room and sends a lovely late cut past backward point for four.
 Eight from the Xavier Bartlett over in total, England building a bit of momentum again here.

 It’s a nice idea, but Banton doesn’t play much red-ball cricket and when he does, he’s in the middle order not opening the batting.
 Luke O’Brien, Auckland 
 12 2 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Eng 231-4 published at 38 overs 38 overs 
 Image source, Getty Images Well, after that excellent century from Tom Banton, we want to know if you think he is worthy of consideration for a Test call-up?
 You can cast your vote at the top of this page (give it a quick refresh if you can't see the poll).
 My view (I know, nobody asked)? Picking players for the Test side based on white-ball form is always a risky business. Jason Roy was brilliant for England in ODIs for years. His stint in the red-ball team was rather less successful.
 Anyway, seven come from Riley Meredith's over in ones and twos.
 10 6 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 How's stat?! published at 06:26 GMT 06:26 GMT 
 Image source, Getty Images Tom Banton fell just five runs short of his highest ODI score. However, this was a much more controlled knock from Banton, with a false-shot percentage of just 7%, compared to 17% during his century against Sri Lanka in September.
 Today, he attacked 64% of the time and defended just 10% of the deliveries. In contrast, during his previous hundred, he attacked 52% of the time and defended 25% of the deliveries.
 15 4 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Eng 224-4 published at 37 overs 37 overs 
 Steady over all round as England take six from Xavier Bartlett.
 Jordan Cox is starting to tick over nicely, he's got 19 at a run a ball and has the potential to really explode later in the innings.
 That's what England will be after but, with 13 overs left in the innings, they'll know they can't really afford to lose another wicket now so both Cox and Will Jacks will need to show a little restraint.

 Post published at 06:20 GMT 06:20 GMT 
 The best scoreboard in world cricket?
 Image source, Getty Images 
 79 9 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Eng 218-4 published at 36 overs 36 overs 
 An all-run four!
 Jordan Cox muscles the ball leg side, it isn't out of the middle but it just keeps going and, while it is eventually pulled back just before the rope, the England pair sprint back for four anyway.
 Two singles round out the over, the second pushed into the covers by Will Jacks to get him off the mark.

 Use the form on this page 
 Why isn’t Tom Banton mentioned as a possible opener in the Test team? Only one of the top five not in the Test team and is in great form!
 Rob Smith, Knebworth 
 54 16 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Eng 212-4 published at 35 overs 35 overs 
 Will Jacks comes in to join Jordan Cox.
 Two relatively new batters at the crease. This is an opportunity for Australia.
 7 10 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 06:15 GMT 06:15 GMT 
 Michael Vaughan 
Former England captain on Test Match Special 
 A fantastic innings from Tom Banton. He went for three from three - you can see why because the previous two balls ended up in the stand.
 Xavier Bartlett just rolled his fingers down the side of the ball and it was a good catch from Cameron Green, who does not drop too many.
 That's a huge wicket for Australia. If they get another few in the next few overs they will be looking at restricting England to 310 or 315.
 9 7 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 WICKET published at 34.5 overs 34.5 overs 
 Banton c Green b Bartlett 121 (Eng 212-4) 
 Image source, Getty Images Tom Banton falls trying for a third six on the bounce.
 He doesn't get enough on this one and Cameron Green dives forward to take an excellent catch at deep mid-wicket.
 Did he really need to go again? Perhaps not but Banton had gone past 100, was batting very nicely and clearly fancied his chances.
 The end of a superb innings and England, potentially, in a bit of a tricky spot.
 17 63 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Eng 212-3 published at 34.4 overs 34.4 overs 
 Pulled dismissively over square leg by Tom Banton!
 Xavier Bartlett bangs one in short but he's not got the pace to trouble the England opener and the ball flies over the rope.
 And again! More of a hook than a pull this time from Banton but the result is the same, six more.
 36 1 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 How's stat?! published at 06:07 GMT 06:07 GMT 
 Image source, Getty Images Harry Brook has a strike-rate of 257 while playing the scoop shot. However, he has also been dismissed three times playing that shot, averaging just 18.
 He has lost his wicket once every seven balls while attempting the scoop. Against pace bowlers, no other shot has resulted in his dismissal as frequently.
 7 15 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Eng 198-3 published at 34 overs 34 overs 
 It certainly felt like a bit of a freebie for Australia, Arjun. It's all about risk and reward with this England team and, so early in his innings, it feels like Harry Brook didn't get the balance quite right.
 It's not the first time he's got into trouble with that ramp shot either.
 15 3 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 get involved Get Involved published at 06:04 GMT 06:04 GMT 
 Use the form on this page 
 Brook just too casual with his wicket at the moment. What a gift for the Aussies.
 Arjun Singh, Edmonton 
 48 4 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Banton holds England together - what you've missed published at 06:03 GMT 06:03 GMT 
 Image source, Getty Images Need a catch-up? Tom Banton is holding England together with his second one-day international century. 
 The opener has been superb. After Ben Duckett was out early, he put on a steady 137 with Joe Root. 
 Root was caught off a leading edge for 62 and Harry Brook bowled attempting a ramp to push the scoring on for five, but Banton has continued to 107 not out.
 England will be eyeing a score over 300 but Banton will need support.
 14 0 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Eng 194-3 published at 33 overs 33 overs 
 Some less than impressive fielding from Travis Head at long-on, just assuming England would settle for a single.
 His lackadaisical approach is spotted by Jordan Cox, though, and he sprints back to earn Tom Banton a second for his lofted drive.
 Cox adds four of his own later in the over with a gorgeous straight drive back past Riley Meredith making it 10 from the over.
